chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subbah al-Kinanī, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What do you think if a man enters into the state of Ihram after a prescribed prayer, would that suffice for him?' He said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.أَحْرَمَ: Entered the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)
key_terms.يُجْزِيهِ: Would suffice / be acceptable for him

ai.seo_question: Can one enter Ihram right after finishing a regular prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Sahih al-Tusi highlights the flexibility in the timing of Ihram, affirming that one may enter the state of consecration immediately after completing a mandatory prayer without needing a separate, distinct intention or time gap. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that the validity of the ritual act is not contingent upon a specific temporal separation from other acts of worship, provided the core intention is present.
